limitations: All new screens are unconverged; EW stability is not full population convergence.
Atomic completeness and realistic collision rates remain unresolved.
OP tables cover selected levels; high levels still use approximate cross-sections.
Fe test includes LTE ground bound-free opacity only; no Fe/Ni line forest or thermal feedback.
Ni continuum screen could not be run: cached Ni IV+ ionization energies and Verner fits absent.
No diffusion equilibrium or levitation-modified abundance profile was imposed.

validation.command: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=src:research python -m pytest -q tests/test_hot_trace_metals.py tests/test_hot_trace_checkpoint.py tests/test_hot_daz_benchmark.py tests/test_hot_daz_comparison.py tests/test_hot_trace_levitation.py tests/test_hot_public.py tests/test_light_metal_nlte.py
new_checks: Warm starts conserve represented particles and do not inherit convergence
Callback spectra are evaluated states and stopping does not grant convergence
Real C III/C IV OP tables preserve Planck detailed balance and Kirchhoff law
Frozen H/He reuse rejects changes to host equations or physical tables
All eight comparison FITS files preserve convergence flags, pass checksums, and round-trip intrinsic predictions exactly

interpretation: C III/C IV atom size has a much larger effect on the C III multiplet than adding the next ion stage did.
Tabulated photoionization data weaken C III at fixed atom size; choosing approximate cross-sections solely for a better observed match is unjustified.
At 120/150 C III/C IV levels with partial OP tables, the two cleaner C III equivalent widths reach 73.9/74.3 percent of observation, versus 45.6/46.6 percent in the baseline.
The selected 80/100 atom reaches about 78 percent with approximate photoionization; LTE Fe continuum changes that by about 2 percent relative.
New spectra are not converged or atom-complete; these are decisions about promising experiments, not fitted abundances or a levitation solution.
